thread:
elaine: heads up — noticed a parity bug: REST /routes/signature returns `signature_required: false` but our TypeScript SDK's Route type drops that field so the onboarding flow shows the signature UI for everyone.
sam: can you paste the curl + SDK output?
elaine: repro: 
```
# REST
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/rt-45 | jq
# => {"id":"rt-45", "path":"/submit", "signature_required": false}

# SDK (ts)
const r = await client.routes.get('rt-45')
// => { id: 'rt-45', path: '/submit' } // signatureRequired missing
```
charlie: likely same truthy-filter bug in serializer (if (v) acc[camel(k)] = v).
elaine: yep grep shows utils.camelizeFilter uses `if (val)`; that drops false. Caused an onboarding UX regression — users were prompted for signature when route didn’t need it.
ci-bot: failing test sampleapp/tests/onboard/test_route_signature.py::test_no_signature_prompt - 1 failed.
sam: fix: change filter to check undefined/null only (`if (val !== null && val !== undefined)`) and add unit + e2e tests for falsy booleans and zeros. Also add a short docs note: REST fields are snake_case and SDK maps to camelCase but must preserve explicit falsy values.
elaine: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1620 with small fix + tests. Will update sampleapp quickstart afterwards.
charlie: nice, LGTM once CI passes. Also add a repo scan for `if (val)` patterns across sdks. I filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/236 (falsy-filter-scan).
ci-bot: CI queued for sdk/pull/1620.
elaine: thanks — will backport if it hits maintenance branch.
